status: G5 first batch: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g5-fascines, in Chapters IX and XII (the desktop app only)
use: Roman siege works behind the line: fascines and gabions beyond the board's west edge, where the Romans attack a wall (Chapters IX and XII).

generator.prompt: Roman siege stores: a low pile of fascines, long tight bundles of brushwood bound with withies, and beside it three gabions, tall cylindrical baskets of woven wicker filled with earth; about three metres long, one point five metres deep and one point two metres high. Dry brushwood, wicker and earth. Single isolated static prop for a grounded painterly-realistic historical game set in the third century Roman world. Physically based aged materials, believable hand-made construction and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above, restrained surface detail, level base and complete geometry from every side. No environment, ground plane, decorative display plinth, modern materials, text, logos or people.

budget.note: Raised at review from 3,500 triangles and 260,000 bytes: its separate sticks stop collapsing at about 3,590 triangles, and only at 6,000 do its gabions keep their round baskets (at 3,590 they crumple into lumps).

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the battles in the desktop build at High
review.notes: A pile of brushwood fascines bound with withies beside four wicker gabions packed with earth, as asked, on a low timber pallet the request did not ask for (it reads as a stores platform). At 3,500 triangles its gabions crumpled into lumps (its separate sticks stop collapsing near 3,590), so its budget was raised to 6,000 triangles and 380,000 bytes.
